tldr: Missing potential-outcome pairing prevents identification of the actual variance of an experimental marginal-Gini contrast. The theorem-level kernel is a global Kolmogorov modulus for the ordered rank-one reward \(C_{a,b}\), depending only on bounded score variation and covering every support and order contact. Establishing that theorem yields a total observed-support estimator of the realizable sharp MTR completion \(T_N\), matched \(N^{-1/2}\) mean absolute error against every labeled-record randomized procedure, finite-assignment upper certificates, and uniform conservative Wald coverage for \(\Delta_N\). The contribution is the general BV/CDF stability theorem and its complete precision application; universal constants are deliberately loose.
gap: Directional transport identifies extremal dependence for particular cost classes, while empirical transport theory controls dual classes under regular cost assumptions. The checked literature does not supply a two-marginal Kolmogorov modulus for arbitrary BV score products under a hard order constraint at all contacts.
fill: The structural theorem derives bounded optimal duals with controlled variation from primitive ordered feasibility. An explicit empirical-CDF projection, a small-mean fallback and finite transport certification translate it into total root-\(N\) completion learning and conservative fixed-table inference.
